_comment: Fine paper at last -- it had no recipe at all before this and could only be bought from a writer.
Pulp, water and two minerals, and **the wood is the reason the minerals are there**. Fine paper was
never wood in our own world: it was linen and cotton rag, and wood pulp is what newsprint is made of
-- lignin-rich and acid, so it yellows, it embrittles, and it feathers a line. What turns pulp into
writing paper is a mineral loading, chalk in the real craft, which buys three things at once: opacity,
a surface smooth enough to take a fine line, and the alkaline reserve that lets a sheet last centuries.
Astrite is that loading, and the fiction is the seismograph's own argument -- a page meant to hold a
world is buffered with the one thing that is of no world.
Deretheni is the danger material, which design 7.1.1 asks both mid-tier rungs to carry so that it stays
load-bearing rather than a midgame reward the endgame walks past.
Stripped logs rather than logs: bark comes off before pulping, being mostly lignin and specks.
The bucket comes back empty on its own -- vanilla gives it as the crafting remainder.
Shapeless, because this is a vat and an arrangement would imply otherwise.
Ratios have had no balancing thought.
